 Chelsea frustrated as Hacken hold on in goalless draw
 Match Summary
 Tue 10 Nov 2026 ‧ UEFA Women's Champions League - League Stage Häcken 0 , Chelsea 0 at Full time Häcken Häcken Häcken 0 0 Chelsea Chelsea Chelsea Full time FT Half Time Häcken 0 , Chelsea 0 HT 0-0 Venue: Nordic Wellness Arena Report (active) 
 Scores 
 Tables 
 Line-ups 
 Match Stats 
 Head-to-head 
 Live Text 
 Figure caption, Chelsea play out goalless draw with Hacken
 Chelsea maintained their unbeaten start in the Women's Champions League but were left frustrated by a goalless draw at Hacken. 
 Boss Sonia Bompastor made six changes to the side held to a 1-1 draw by Everton and the Blues failed to find their rhythm in a disappointing attacking performance against a side who picked up their second point in this season's competition.
 Hacken were well organised throughout and held on despite Chelsea ramping up the pressure in the closing stages.
 Their best chance in that period came in the 71st minute when substitute Manaka Matsukubo raced on to a ball following a corner for the hosts and found Alyssa Thompson, who skipped past goalkeeper Jennifer Falk but had her shot cleared off the line.
 Ellie Carpenter's relentless running caused problems down the right, but her side failed to make the most of the 16 crossing chances she created, although Maika Hamano did clip the top of the bar from an assist from the Australian.
 With eight points from their four games, Chelsea moved up to second in the standings behind Barcelona before Tuesday's late games.
 They thought they had taken the lead on two separate occasions in the first half through Wieke Kaptein and Melvine Malard only to be denied by the offside flag.
 As Hacken showed defiant defence to keep them at bay, the hosts almost snatched a late winner of their own.
 With three minutes left Maja Bodin got clear of Veerle Buurman, but pressure from the Chelsea defender meant she could not get the shot off with accuracy and Liv Peng was able to save.
 Bompaster - who received a yellow card late in the game - had been hoping for a better showing from her side following the draw against Everton. 
 But Hacken held firm, although they are still searching for their first win in Europe this season.
 More to follow.
